dek: A Las Vegas handicapper who says he founded Logical Approach in 1982 and still runs it alone. short_answer: Andy Iskoe is a real, long running Las Vegas handicapper. His Logical Approach site names him as founder and sole proprietor, gives a Las Vegas post office box, phone and email, and on 17 Nov 2026 offered 2026 football subscriptions and a free selection dated 12 Nov 2026. A 2001 Daily Racing Form article called him one of the most respected sports analysts in town. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is a separate question. The site lists contest finishes and highlights, such as a 14 for 14 week in a 2002 newspaper column, but we found no full, time stamped log of every premium play that we could check.

His pitch is unusually low key: one service, everyone gets the same plays, no lock games, and it admits to losing seasons. Independent buyer talk is almost absent, and the one forum thread we found, from 2010, criticized a long running article of his on baseball run lines.

The form says current prices hold through the end of the season and cover the rest of the regular season, the bowls and the NFL playoffs. Payment is by card, check, money order or PayPal.

guarantee: The 2026 order form and the 2026 service page state no guarantee, credit or refund terms. Subscriptions are sold only for the full season or the balance of the season.

An older Logical Approach order page from November 2008 is still online. It offered an $49.95 weekend of 11 plays with a promise that at least 7 would cover "OR YOU GET ALL OF OUR PREMIUM COLLEGE & PRO SELECTIONS NEXT WEEK ... AT NO CHARGE." That offer is not current, and it paid in more picks, not money.
Nothing covers your losses on the bets themselves.

claims_note: The time figures do not line up. The same page says he founded the service in 1982, that it has run "for all of its 41 years," that he has done this "for almost 40 years, the last 33 of which he's been based in Las Vegas," and that 2026 is his 36th football season in Las Vegas after moving in 1991. The copy looks like it has been carried forward year to year without updating.

The highlights are single weeks and contest finishes, some more than 20 years old. They show he has had strong stretches, not how a full season of premium plays has done. To its credit, the page says "we've had an occasional losing season as well" and warns readers to avoid anyone selling lock games.
Parts of the site are plainly stale. The home page still links a future book odds section marked "Odds Updated June 29, 2020," and an order page from 2008 is still online.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find for recent seasons. We found no full, time stamped log of every Logical Approach premium play with the line and release time, and no court or regulator record about the service.

What the seller publishes: a daily complimentary selection (on 17 Nov 2026 the page showed one dated 12 Nov 2026, a college football over), contest finishes, the 2002 and 2001 highlights above, and a 2008 season figure on an old order page.

One unverified outside figure exists: in a 2010 Las Vegas Advisor forum thread, one member wrote, while asking to be corrected, that a monitoring service had his adjusted lifetime record at about 51% against the spread. Nobody sourced it, and we could not check it.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Andy Iskoe or Logical Approach pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Andy Iskoe performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the only season figure on his site is 59.1% from 2008, and the only outside figure we saw is an unsourced 51% lifetime claim from a 2010 forum post. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Andy Iskoe is very thin. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no buyer reviews of Logical Approach subscriptions at all: no comments on review sites, no Reddit posts and no recent forum threads. The outside material is about the man rather than the service. A 2001 Daily Racing Form article described him as one of the most respected sports analysts in Las Vegas. A 2010 Las Vegas Advisor forum thread, started by a well known bettor, criticized a run line betting article he had repeated for years, and one poster passed on an unsourced claim of about 51% lifetime against the spread; another member declined to join the criticism. Nothing we found involves billing, refunds or non delivery.

In a Las Vegas Advisor baseball forum thread titled "Someone please call Andy Iskoe and explain Run Line Betting," several members argued that his long running advice to play big favorites on the run line ignored how sportsbooks price those bets. One member repeated an unsourced figure of about 51% lifetime against the spread. One other member said he was not into criticism and shared his own run line results. This is about his public writing, not his paid plays.

Reddit archive searches for Iskoe in r/sportsbetting and r/sportsbook, and for Logical Approach in r/SportsBettingPicks, returned nothing about him. Our web searches found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread about the service, and no review site page with buyer comments.

conflicts: We found no sportsbook affiliate links on the Logical Approach pages we read.

Logical Approach also offers paid proxy services for Las Vegas football contests, according to its 2026 contest page. That is a separate business line, not a conflict with the picks, but a buyer should know the site sells more than selections.
strengths: A named operator with a Las Vegas mailing address, phone and email on the order form.
One service with the same plays for every client, published flat season prices, and no lock or 80% claims.
The sales page admits to losing seasons.
Independent press coverage exists, though old: a 2001 Daily Racing Form article.
concerns: No full public record of premium plays for any recent season.
Highlights are single weeks and contest finishes, many over 20 years old.
Year counts on the sales page contradict each other, and parts of the site are years out of date.
No guarantee, credit or refund terms appear on the 2026 order form.
Season only subscriptions mean you pay up front for the rest of the season.
checklist: Ask for every premium play from the last full season with the line and the time it was sent. Contest finishes are not a record.
Count units, not wins. Double plays and single plays carry different weight.
Ask in writing what happens if you are unhappy, since the order form states no refund terms.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running Las Vegas handicapper with a named business, a mailing address and a phone number, and he was described in a 2001 Daily Racing Form article as a respected analyst. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, because he does not publish a full record, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Andy Iskoe cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 the order form listed one football newsletter at $75, all three at $100, the Premium Late Selection Service at $300 and the premium service with all three newsletters at $425, each for the balance of the season.
Does Andy Iskoe have a verified record?
No. His site lists contest finishes, a 14 for 14 week from 2002 and a 2008 season figure of 59.1%. We found no independent, time stamped log of every premium play.

For a flat season price you get every newsletter play and premium play, plus the right to call or email him with questions. What is unproven is whether the plays beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over a full season, and no guarantee or refund is stated.
